notes: Sourced from NewTek's own 2014 "3Play 4800" one-sheet/datasheet (branded NewTek, mirrored via AV-iQ's document CDN) for feature/spec text, cross-verified against the official NewTek 3Play family User Manual (rev. April 12, 2013, covers 3Play 4800/820/330 sharing this backplate) which includes a labeled, photographed rear-panel diagram (Figure 7) that was used to confirm exact connector counts/shapes, and against NewTek Knowledge Base articles and B&H/Adorama/HighwayAV listings (all consistent). The current live manufacturer page (https://www.newtek.com/3play/4800/) confirms the product listing but its tech-specs subpage returned 404 at fetch time; the German tech-specs URL surfaced in search (de.newtek.com) did not resolve. Video In/Out are physically multi-format BNC groups (1 SDI BNC + 3 analog BNC for Y/Pb/Pr, reused for Component/Y-C/Composite) - modeled here as 8 input + 3 output combo ports (connector "sdi", accepts "bnc") rather than exploding into 44 individual BNC jacks. AES3/EBU digital audio rides on 75-ohm BNC (not XLR) per the actual panel. Two connectors have no exact match in the provided connector-id list: the "Tally" port is a 2-row DB-15 D-sub (mapped to "vga" as the closest shape, but it is not a VGA video signal and this pin is documented as reserved/inactive) and the "eSATA" storage port (mapped to "usb-a" as the closest bidirectional data connector). HDMI version and USB version are not stated anywhere in NewTek's documentation and were inferred (medium/low confidence) from the product's ~2012-2014 hardware generation. Video/SDI grade (sdi-hd) is high-confidence, explicitly sourced from the manual's "HD-SDI video conforms to SMPTE 292M" statement. A Multi-Standard model variant additionally supports PAL/NTSC-J session formats but has identical physical I/O to the NTSC-only model. Ethernet is a single physical Gigabit RJ45 port serving both network A/V output (to TriCaster) and Gigabit overlay network inputs.

ports.name: HDMI Out
ports.note: Tracks the active playout channel delegate (A or B). HDMI version not stated in NewTek docs; 1.4 inferred from ~2012-2014 hardware era and stated max output of 1920x1080.

ports.name: Display Out (HDMI)
ports.note: One of two supplemental 'Display' outputs; video-only HDMI with independent color control, used for auxiliary monitoring. Panel silkscreen labels it '(5) DISPLAY'. HDMI version inferred, not stated.

ports.name: Multiview Out
ports.note: Panel-labeled 'MULTIVIEW'. Manual confirms DVI-D (digital only); cannot drive analog/VGA-only displays.

ports.name: Display Out (VGA)
ports.note: Second supplemental 'Display' output (panel labels it '(6) DISPLAY'), blue HD15/VGA connector, for auxiliary monitoring with independent color control.

ports.name: Interface Out
ports.note: Drives the external Windows GUI monitor for the built-in PC. Manual says 'use an adapter if necessary' for analog monitors, implying DVI-I; NewTek does not explicitly state DVI-I vs DVI-D.

ports.name: Tally
ports.note: Panel-labeled DB-15 connector; physically a 2-row D-sub, not a true 3-row VGA/HD15 - mapped to 'vga' as the closest available connector id. Manual states this pin was reserved/inactive; NewTek's tally feature is instead delivered over Ethernet from a companion TriCaster.

ports.name: eSATA
ports.note: Physical connector is eSATA (for external storage/backup drives); no eSATA id exists in the supplied connector list, so 'usb-a' is used as the closest approximation - the real connector shape differs.

ports.name: Ethernet
ports.note: Used for network output of Channel A/B to a NewTek TriCaster and for Gigabit network overlay inputs (iVGA, AirPlay, LiveText, etc.).

ports.name: USB 1
ports.note: One of 4 USB ports (keyboard/mouse/peripherals). Version not stated in specs; 2.0 inferred from port color/era.

ports.name: Phones
ports.note: Stereo 1/4-inch headphone monitoring output.

ports.name: AC In 1
ports.note: One of two independent IEC (C13/C14-style) inlets feeding the 550W redundant, hot-swappable/removable power-supply modules; each has its own rocker switch.

ports.name: AC In 2
ports.note: Second redundant IEC power inlet, mirrors AC In 1.

ports.name: Audio In 1a
ports.note: Balanced analog XLR mic/line input (8 groups x 2 = 16 total), software-configurable as Mic w/wo phantom power or Line.

ports.name: Audio In 7a
ports.note: Group 7 also accepts external LTC timecode input per the manual.

ports.name: Audio Out 1a
ports.note: Channel A balanced analog output group (4 XLR: 1a-1d).

ports.name: Audio Out 2a
ports.note: Channel B balanced analog output group (4 XLR: 2a-2d).

ports.name: AES In 1
ports.note: 75-ohm BNC AES3/EBU digital audio input, one per video input group (8 total).

ports.name: AES Out 1ab
ports.note: 75-ohm BNC AES3/EBU digital audio output.

ports.name: Video In 1
ports.note: Multi-format BNC input group (1 of 8): primary HD/SD-SDI BNC (SMPTE 292M, i.e. sdi-hd) plus 3 additional BNC jacks (Y, Pb, Pr) in the same column for HD/SD Component, Y/C (S-Video via adapter), or Composite - modeled as one combo port rather than 4 separate jacks.

ports.name: Video Out 1
ports.note: Channel A primary output group: SDI BNC plus Y/Pb/Pr BNCs (Component, Y/C, or Composite) in the same column.

ports.name: Video Out 2
ports.note: Channel B primary output group, same multi-format layout as Video Out 1.

ports.name: Video Out 3
ports.note: Aux output group - follows whichever of Channel A/B is currently delegated; same multi-format BNC layout.

ports.name: Gen Lock
ports.note: House-sync/reference (black burst) input; locks to HD or SD analog tri-level or bi-level sync. No SDI bandwidth grade applies.
